messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike of GPU nodes failing to join in eu-west-2 after the FW policy change. bootstrap errors show KMS decrypt failures.
ashok: Can you paste the exact error lines from the node agent?
maria: sure, from node-init.log:
```
2024-11-08T10:03:12Z ERROR keystore: decrypt failed status=403 endpoint=https://kms.eu-west-2.internal key-id=alias/infra-gpu-node
2024-11-08T10:03:12Z WARN  node-join: retrying decrypt, attempt=3
2024-11-08T10:03:20Z ERROR node-join: join aborted: bootstrap decrypt failed
```
carmen: That aligns with the firewall rule I pushed this morning (rule id fw-eu-719). I added a deny for outbound 443 to non-whitelisted endpoints. Maybe the KMS endpoint IP isn't in the allowlist.
bob: infra-bot also fired an alert: `ALERT: 38 nodes failed register (eu-west-2) in last 12m` — can we confirm if it's only KMS or other endpoints?
infra-bot: [ALERT] 2024-11-08T10:05:00Z - node-registration-failure - region=eu-west-2 count=38 primary_error=keystore.decrypt_403
oncall-jess: Quick check: can we curl the kms endpoint from a repro host in the same subnet? Also, are we hitting a NAT or proxy that rewrites SNI?
maria: Tried from a failing node container: `curl -v https://kms.eu-west-2.internal/health` -> TLS handshake ok, but `403` returned, headers show `x-auth-reject: firewall`.
ashok: Sounds like the fw appliance is doing deep-packet inspection and rejecting the request, likely because the destination cert or host isn't in the allowlist. Workaround: allowlist the KMS FQDN or the internal IP range used by KMS.
carmen: I rolled the rule out because of audit request to lock egress. We tightened to whitelisted hostnames but apparently the internal KMS is served by dynamic IPs behind a load balancer; we only whitelisted a static IP list for other services. My bad.
bob: Two-fold problem: 1) nodes can't decrypt so join fails -> capacity loss, 2) we tightened audit log retention and S3 lifecycle earlier which affects investigations. We should balance compliance vs availability.
sre-lead: Priority: restore GPU capacity. Proposal: revert fw-eu-719 to previous state for 15m, create a temporary exception for `kms.eu-west-2.internal` DNS name in the fw, then roll a stable allowlist keyed off the KMS ALIAS.
oncall-jess: Also prepare a canary procedure: bring up 3 nodes in a test pool, confirm join. If green, scale a controlled rehealing.
carmen: I'll open a rollback PR now and add a follow-up to do a hostname-based exception. tagging @maria to validate.
maria: ACK, after rollback I'll trigger node re-register (`kubectl taint node ...` + restart agent) and post results.
bob: We should also consider a longer-term change: our fw should allow outbound to internal AWS-managed endpoints (KMS/STS/metadata) via FQDN, not IP snapshots. Otherwise dynamic infra will keep breaking.
ashok: Agree. Also: audit/logging tradeoff — keeping full VPC flow logs for 90d is $$$. For investigations like this we only need 30d hot logs + long-term compressed. I'll draft a proposal for tiered retention to reduce cost.
sre-lead: Action items:
- carmen: rollback rule for 15m + create PR for hostname exception (ETA 10m)
- maria: validate node rejoin and post success/failure (ETA 20m)
- oncall-jess: run canary and monitor infra-bot alerts (ETA 30m)
- ashok: prepare a small runbook snippet for KMS-decrypt-failure -> fw-check -> rollback steps (ETA EOD)
- bob: draft retention tier plan for audit logs and cost estimate (ETA tomorrow)
carmen: rollback PR created -> https://git.internal/r/fw/pulls/1287 (rolling back fw-eu-719 for eu-west-2). Reverting now.
maria: After revert: `infra-bot` shows node registration recovering, first batch of 12 nodes rejoined.
infra-bot: [RESOLVED] 2024-11-08T10:18:00Z - node-registration-failure - region=eu-west-2 resolved_count=12 remaining=26
oncall-jess: Canary start: provisioning 3 test GPU nodes in eu-west-2 -> join ok for two, one still failing with decrypt 403 (same pattern). Investigating that node's subnet.
maria: That node was in a different private subnet with a firewall appliance chain. Opening a ticket to network owners to add KMS FQDN there.
bob: Good work. Once all canaries green, we should roll the healed pool and then re-evaluate fw rule design. Also keep security in the loop; we don't want to re-open broad egress and break compliance.
sre-lead: Summary: immediate revert applied, partial recovery underway. Longer term: move to FQDN-aware egress policies, tiered audit retention, and a small canary pool test before egress hardening. I'll follow up in a doc. Thanks all :thumbsup:
